```{r}
#| label: setup
#| include: false

suppressPackageStartupMessages({
  library(ggplot2)
  library(knitr)
})

kOutputDir <- file.path("..", "output", "vanderbeke2021")

ReadOutput <- function(name) {
  path <- file.path(kOutputDir, name)
  if (!file.exists(path)) {
    stop(
      "The analysis output is missing: ", path, "\n",
      "Run scripts/11_vanderbeke2021_covid.R first. ",
      "See the section 'Reproducing this'."
    )
  }
  read.csv(path, check.names = FALSE)
}

OutputImage <- function(name) {
  file.path(kOutputDir, name)
}

verdicts <- ReadOutput("claim_verdicts.csv")
```

## Introduction

Vanderbeke and colleagues reported monocyte-driven atypical cytokine storm and
aberrant neutrophil activation as key mediators of COVID-19 disease severity
[1]. The deposit carries 49 flow cytometry files across three clinical groups,
with a FlowJo workspace that gates every sample. This report compares the
deposited manual gates against an automated density-based rule on the five
lineage populations.

```{r}
#| label: design

kable(
  ReadOutput("design.csv"),
  caption = "The cohort, read from the file names.",
  col.names = c("Group", "Files")
)
```

```{r}
#| label: panel

panel <- ReadOutput("panel.csv")
named <- panel[nzchar(trimws(panel$marker)) & trimws(panel$marker) != "-", ]
kable(
  data.frame(Marker = paste(named$marker, collapse = ", ")),
  caption = "Every named marker of the 34 colour panel."
)
```

The panel carries the lineage markers, the naive and memory markers, the
checkpoint markers and a set of cytokines and transcription factors, which is
what an intracellular cytokine panel needs.

```{r}
#| label: headers

headers <- ReadOutput("file_headers.csv")
kable(
  data.frame(
    Measure = c("Files", "Cytometer", "Fluorescence channels",
                "Smallest file, events", "Median file, events",
                "Largest file, events", "Files above 500,000 events"),
    Value = c(
      nrow(headers), unique(headers$cytometer),
      unique(headers$compensated_channels),
      format(min(headers$total_events), big.mark = ","),
      format(stats::median(headers$total_events), big.mark = ","),
      format(max(headers$total_events), big.mark = ","),
      sum(headers$total_events > 5e5)
    )
  ),
  caption = "The deposit, read from the FCS headers."
)
```

## Methods

### The dataset

The cohort comprises 49 files across three clinical groups. The FlowJo workspace
gates every sample. Each file was exported after a live cell gate and every
fluorescence channel is compensated.

### Preprocessing

No preprocessing was applied. The deposited files were used as exported.

### Gating

The manual arm is the deposited workspace, applied to the deposited files by
CytoML. No gate was refit. The automated arm uses a density minimum with a two
component mixture as the fallback, fitted on each file. Both arms count the same
five populations with the same denominators. CD3 is a percentage of the exported
live cells. CD4 and CD8 are percentages of CD3. CD14 and CD19 sit beside CD3
rather than under it, which is the shape the workspace uses.

### Statistics

Spearman correlation measures agreement between arms across files. The median
difference between arms is reported for each measure. Group comparisons use the
Mann-Whitney test for COVID-19 against healthy and the Kruskal-Wallis test
between the two COVID-19 groups.

### Software

The analysis uses CytoML, flowCore, ggplot2 and knitr. Every version is pinned
in the container.

## Part 1: six patients who changed group after the workspace was written

```{r}
#| label: relabelled

relabelled <- ReadOutput("relabelled_patients.csv")
kable(
  relabelled[, c("patient", "group")],
  caption = "The six files whose name carries ICU_changedW.",
  col.names = c("Patient", "Group in the file name")
)
```

Six deposited files are named `ICU_changedW`, where the workspace still names
the same sample `W`. Those six patients moved from the ward to intensive care
after the workspace was built, and the file name records the move while the
workspace does not. A join on the file name therefore drops six of the 49
samples, and it drops them silently. The join key removes the marker, so both
arms meet on all of them.

## Part 2: the two arms

Both arms count the same five populations on the files that both measured.

```{r}
#| label: cut-rules

kable(
  ReadOutput("cut_rule_summary.csv"),
  caption = "Which rule placed each automated cut.",
  col.names = c("Marker", "Rule", "Cuts")
)
```

```{r}
#| label: agreement

kable(
  ReadOutput("arm_agreement.csv"),
  digits = 3,
  caption = "The deposited gates against the automated rule, on the files that both arms measured.",
  col.names = c("Measure", "Files", "Manual median", "Automated median",
                "Median difference", "Spearman rho", "p")
)
```

```{r}
#| label: comparison-figure
#| fig-cap: "Each point is one file. The dashed line is equality."

knitr::include_graphics(OutputImage("arm_comparison.png"))
```

CD3, CD8 and CD14 all correlate above rho 0.94 across the files, and the median
difference between the two arms stays inside four percentage points on every
measure. CD4 and CD19 correlate less well, at about rho 0.77, and both are the measures
where the two arms also disagree most in the median.

## Part 3: the claims

```{r}
#| label: by-group

kable(
  ReadOutput("measures_by_group.csv"),
  digits = 3,
  caption = "Every lineage measure by clinical group and by arm. The p values are Mann-Whitney for COVID-19 against healthy and Kruskal-Wallis between the two COVID-19 groups.",
  col.names = c("Measure", "Arm", "Healthy median", "Ward median",
                "Intensive care median", "p, COVID-19 against healthy",
                "p, between severity groups")
)
```

```{r}
#| label: group-figure
#| fig-cap: "The lineage measures by group, with both arms side by side."

knitr::include_graphics(OutputImage("measures_by_group.png"))
```

The paper reports that T helper and cytotoxic T cell counts do not separate the
two COVID-19 severity groups, and the deposited gates agree. It also reports a
higher CD4 over CD8 ratio in COVID-19 than in the healthy controls, most
pronounced in critical disease, and the deposit says the same with the ordering
running the way the paper states it.

```{r}
#| label: functional

kable(
  ReadOutput("functional_by_group.csv"),
  digits = 3,
  caption = "The interferon gamma producing subsets by group, from the automated arm.",
  col.names = c("Measure", "Arm", "Healthy median", "Ward median",
                "Intensive care median", "p, COVID-19 against healthy",
                "p, between severity groups")
)
```

The Th1 subset falls in COVID-19 relative to the healthy controls, in the
direction the paper reports. The difference does not reach significance in this analysis.

```{r}
#| label: pd1

kable(
  ReadOutput("pd1_by_subset.csv"),
  digits = 1,
  caption = "PD-1 positive cells inside each naive and memory subset, from the automated arm.",
  col.names = c("Subset", "Samples", "Median PD-1 positive, percent")
)
```

```{r}
#| label: pd1-figure
#| fig-cap: "PD-1 by subset. The effector subsets sit at the top and the naive subsets at the bottom."

knitr::include_graphics(OutputImage("pd1_by_subset.png"))
```

The paper reports PD-1 high on the effector T cells, with a predominance in CD8
terminally differentiated effector memory cells. The effector part reproduces.
The two effector memory subsets and the two terminally differentiated subsets
carry far more PD-1 than the naive subsets, and the ordering is unambiguous. The
predominance does not, because the highest subset in this analysis is CD8
effector memory rather than CD8 terminally differentiated, so the claim is
recorded as partly reproduced.


## Discussion

### What this shows

On a clean deposit with published boundaries, an automated rule tracks a human
closely. Three of the five lineage measures correlate above rho 0.94 across 48
files, and no median differs by more than four percentage points. The input
rather than the method explains the result. The rule did not change. The
scatter, the viability gate and the compensation were already settled by the
depositors, so the only thing left for the rule to get wrong was the position of
a cut on a bimodal marker, which is the case it handles well. The claims the
paper makes from the flow data hold as well. Four reproduce, and two reproduce
in direction without reaching significance on six healthy controls.

### Where the two arms part company

CD4 and CD19 are the loose pair, both correlating at about rho 0.77 where the
others exceed 0.94. CD4 in this panel sits on a BUV496 detector and CD19 on
BV480, and both are read inside a 34 colour panel where the spread from
neighbouring detectors is largest. A cut on a marker with a wide negative
shoulder moves further for a small change in rule than a cut on a clean bimodal
marker. The disagreement is a boundary disagreement and not a population
disagreement, and the two arms rank the samples the same way, which is what the
correlation says.

### What this does not show

This report does not show that the automated rule would work on the raw files.
The deposit is exported after a live cell gate, so the scatter, viability and
compensation steps were never attempted here. It also does not test the cytokine
claims that the paper draws from mass cytometry or from single cell sequencing,
because those data sit in other accessions and in GEO. The healthy group holds
six samples, so every comparison against it in this report is underpowered, and
the report says so rather than reading a p value above 0.05 as an absence of an
effect.

### What is left to do

The workspace gates five populations, and the panel carries twenty more markers,
including the cytokines that the paper's argument rests on, none of them gated
in the deposited workspace. An automated route is the only way to reach them.
The six relabelled patients should also be checked against the paper's own group
assignment before their clinical group is used in anything further.

## Reproducing this

```bash
# Pull this dataset only, 872 MB of the 103 GB archive
./sync.sh pull datasets/flowrepository/FR-FCM-Z2KP

# Build the container. Every package version is pinned and asserted at build time.
./containers/build.sh

# The analysis
podman run --rm -v "$PWD:/work:z" -w /work everything-flow-cytometry:latest \
  Rscript scripts/11_vanderbeke2021_covid.R

# This report
podman run --rm -v "$PWD:/work:z" -w /work everything-flow-cytometry:latest \
  quarto render reports/vanderbeke2021_covid.qmd
```

The manual arm needs the deposited workspace, which travels with the files in
`attachments/`. The claims live in `gating/vanderbeke2021_paper_claims.csv`,
each with the sentence it came from.

```{r}
#| label: session-info

sessionInfo()
```
